title: MITCHELL-RILEY SYNDROME
alt_titles: DIABETES, NEONATAL, WITH PANCREATIC HYPOPLASIA, INTESTINAL ATRESIA, AND GALLBLADDER APLASIA OR HYPOPLASIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Mitchell-Riley syndrome (MTCHRS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the RFX6 gene (612659) on chromosome 6q22.

checks.claim: Mitchell-Riley syndrome (MTCHRS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the RFX6 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Proband #3, still alive at the age of 9 and intermittently off insulin, was a compound heterozygote for donor-site loss in intron 6 (IVS6+2 t>g) and disruption of the acceptor site in intron 1 (IVS1-12 a>g).
checks.explanation: The other probands carried homozygous mutations, and the paper proposes the name Mitchell-Riley syndrome for this condition.

checks.claim: The RFX6 gene is located on chromosome 6q22.
checks.evidence_quote: Of these genes, only RFX6, which falls in the largest segment at 6q21-22, had pancreas–enriched expression
checks.explanation: The paper places RFX6 in the 6q21-22 segment. Giving its standard cytogenetic location as 6q22 is compatible with this.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell-Riley syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder that presents in the neonatal period. Its main features are neonatal diabetes mellitus with a hypoplastic or annular pancreas, intestinal atresia (duodenal, jejunal, or both), and aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder. Some patients have intestinal malrotation, biliary abnormalities, and chronic diarrhea or malabsorption.

checks.claim: Mitchell-Riley syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome involving a genetic abnormality that interferes with normal islet development
checks.explanation: The authors conclude that the condition is probably autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Mitchell-Riley syndrome presents in the neonatal period.
checks.evidence_quote: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia.
checks.explanation: All five patients presented as infants with neonatal diabetes.

checks.claim: A main feature of Mitchell-Riley syndrome is neonatal diabetes mellitus.
checks.evidence_quote: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas
checks.explanation: Neonatal diabetes is one of the core features described.

checks.claim: A main feature of Mitchell-Riley syndrome is a hypoplastic or annular pancreas.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: A hypoplastic or annular pancreas is listed as a feature.

checks.claim: A main feature of Mitchell-Riley syndrome is intestinal atresia, which may be duodenal, jejunal, or both.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: Both jejunal and duodenal atresia are listed.

checks.claim: A main feature of Mitchell-Riley syndrome is aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder.
checks.evidence_quote: jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: Aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder is listed.

checks.claim: Some patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome have intestinal malrotation.
checks.evidence_quote: low birth weight, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas and intestinal malrotation
checks.explanation: The patient with Martínez-Frías syndrome (the same disorder as Mitchell-Riley syndrome) had intestinal malrotation.

checks.claim: Some patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome have biliary abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: low birthweight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias
checks.explanation: The sibs had extrahepatic biliary atresia, which is a biliary abnormality.

checks.claim: Some patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome have chronic diarrhea or malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: In addition, the syndrome involves hypoplastic gall bladder, and intractable diarrhea unresponsive to pancreatic enzyme replacement.
checks.explanation: The paper describes intractable diarrhea and, in the Discussion, severe intestinal malabsorption.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell et al. (2004) described 5 infants with a new syndrome of neonatal diabetes, a hypoplastic or annular pancreas, duodenal or jejunal atresia, and aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder. Some were born to consanguineous parents, which pointed to autosomal recessive inheritance. Intrauterine growth retardation was present, and several of the infants died in early life.

checks.claim: Mitchell et al. (2004) described 5 infants with a new syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Five clinical cases are described.
checks.explanation: The paper describes five infants and presents the condition as a new syndrome.

checks.claim: The 5 infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) had neonatal diabetes.
checks.evidence_quote: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes
checks.explanation: All five infants had neonatal diabetes.

checks.claim: The 5 infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) had a hypoplastic or annular pancreas.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas
checks.explanation: The infants had a hypoplastic or annular pancreas.

checks.claim: The 5 infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) had duodenal or jejunal atresia.
checks.evidence_quote: hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: Jejunal and duodenal atresia are both reported.

checks.claim: The 5 infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) had aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder.
checks.evidence_quote: jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: Gallbladder aplasia or hypoplasia is reported.

checks.claim: Some of the infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) were born to consanguineous parents.
checks.evidence_quote: One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents.
checks.explanation: Two of the infants (one sibling pair) had consanguineous parents.

checks.claim: The consanguinity among the infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) suggested autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome
checks.explanation: The authors do propose autosomal recessive inheritance. The abstract mentions consanguinity, but it does not say that this was the basis for the conclusion; affected sibling pairs could also have contributed.

checks.claim: Intrauterine growth retardation was present in the infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention intrauterine growth retardation. Only the abstract was supplied.

checks.claim: Several of the infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) died in early life.
checks.evidence_quote: Four children died in the first year of life despite aggressive medical management.
checks.explanation: Four of the five infants died in their first year.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell-Riley syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. Mitchell et al. (2004) suggested this from the occurrence in consanguineous families. Smith et al. (2010) confirmed it when they found biallelic RFX6 mutations in affected individuals.

checks.claim: Mitchell-Riley syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome
checks.explanation: The paper proposes autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Mitchell et al. (2004) suggested autosomal recessive inheritance of Mitchell-Riley syndrome based on its occurrence in consanguineous families.
checks.evidence_quote: One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents.
checks.explanation: The authors suggest autosomal recessive inheritance, but the abstract reports only one consanguineous family, not several. It also does not say that consanguinity was the basis for the suggestion.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance of Mitchell-Riley syndrome by finding biallelic RFX6 mutations in affected individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: Proband #2, still alive at age 4.5 years, had the homozygous missense mutation 217 Ser>Pro, confirming the unbiased exon sequencing described above. All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.
checks.explanation: Probands carried homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations, each inherited from carrier parents.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2010) found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the RFX6 gene in patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome, including patients from the families reported by Mitchell et al. (2004). They identified the gene by homozygosity mapping in consanguineous families followed by candidate gene sequencing. RFX6 encodes a winged-helix transcription factor. Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 is expressed in the developing gut endoderm and pancreatic endocrine lineage, and that it acts downstream of NGN3 in islet cell development.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found homozygous or compound heterozygous RFX6 mutations in patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q
checks.explanation: The paper also reports a compound heterozygous proband (#3) and a homozygous proband (#2).

checks.claim: The patients with RFX6 mutations studied by Smith et al. (2010) included patients from the families reported by Mitchell et al. (2004).
checks.evidence_quote: autopsies of two cases (proband #1 and case 3 in Ref) revealed normal-appearing exocrine pancreata
checks.explanation: The paper links its probands to earlier clinical case reports and names the syndrome after the clinicians who first described it. However, the citation is an unnamed 'Ref', and the supplied text never explicitly identifies these as the Mitchell et al. (2004) families.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) identified RFX6 as the Mitchell-Riley syndrome gene by homozygosity mapping in consanguineous families followed by candidate gene sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease locus was mapped using overlapping homozygosity in probands #1and #2 (see Supplementary material for pedigree information and references to previous clinical case reports) respectively the offspring of first and second cousins.
checks.explanation: Homozygosity mapping in two consanguineous families was followed by sequencing of RFX6, the candidate gene (alongside deep exon sequencing).

checks.claim: RFX6 encodes a winged-helix transcription factor.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified Rfx6, a member of the RFX (Regulatory Factor X-box binding) family of winged-helix transcription factors.
checks.explanation: The paper states RFX6 is a winged-helix transcription factor.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 is expressed in the developing gut endoderm.
checks.evidence_quote: Rfx6 is expressed initially broadly in the definitive endoderm after gastrulation, becomes restricted to the gut and pancreatic bud at mid gestation
checks.explanation: The paper shows expression in developing gut endoderm.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 is expressed in the pancreatic endocrine lineage.
checks.evidence_quote: demonstrating restricted expression of Rfx6 in the endocrine lineage even at this early stage
checks.explanation: The paper shows expression in the pancreatic endocrine lineage.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 acts downstream of NGN3 in islet cell development.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that the transcription factor Rfx6 directs islet cell differentiation downstream of Neurog3.
checks.explanation: NGN3 is an alias of Neurog3.

paragraphs.text: Later reports described patients with biallelic RFX6 mutations and a milder or variable phenotype. Some lacked intestinal atresia, and in some the diabetes began after the neonatal period.

checks.claim: Reports after the initial description identified patients with biallelic RFX6 mutations and a milder or variable phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: This relatively milder phenotype is reflected in the greater age of survival of the two cases in the present report.
checks.explanation: The paper reports later cases with biallelic RFX6 mutations and a milder phenotype.

checks.claim: Some patients with biallelic RFX6 mutations lacked intestinal atresia.
checks.explanation: Both patients in this paper had intestinal atresia (duodenal atresia), and the paper describes duodenal atresia in all previously reported cases. It reports no patient without intestinal atresia.

checks.claim: In some patients with biallelic RFX6 mutations, diabetes began after the neonatal period.
checks.evidence_quote: These new cases are the first with Mitchell–Riley syndrome in whom the diagnosis of diabetes was not made in the neonatal period
checks.explanation: Diabetes was diagnosed at ages 3 and 6 years.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6-null mice developed hyperglycemia shortly after birth and died. Islet cells, including insulin-producing beta cells, failed to form, except for pancreatic polypeptide-producing cells. In zebrafish, Smith et al. (2010) found that rfx6 was needed for the differentiation of endocrine cells into hormone-producing islet cells.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6-null mice developed hyperglycemia shortly after birth.
checks.explanation: The paper does not report hyperglycemia or blood glucose in the null mice. It reports failure to feed, bowel distension and death within 2 days.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6-null mice died shortly after birth.
checks.evidence_quote: failed to feed normally, exhibited gross bowel distension due to small bowel obstruction (Fig. 3e-f) and died within 2 days post partum.
checks.explanation: The null mice died within 2 days of birth.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found that islet cells, including insulin-producing beta cells, failed to form in Rfx6-null mice.
checks.evidence_quote: Mice lacking Rfx6 failed to generate any of the normal islet cell types except for pancreatic-polypeptide-producing cells.
checks.explanation: Insulin-expressing cells were absent, although endocrine cells without hormones were still present.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found that pancreatic polypeptide-producing cells still formed in Rfx6-null mice.
checks.evidence_quote: Mice lacking Rfx6 failed to generate any of the normal islet cell types except for pancreatic-polypeptide-producing cells.
checks.explanation: The paper says PP cells were present and in fact increased in number.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found that rfx6 is needed in zebrafish for the differentiation of endocrine cells into hormone-producing islet cells.
checks.explanation: The paper contains no zebrafish experiments; it studies only mice and humans.
